1 Executive summary

Use these results to examine connected-tank response and select the measurements needed before design application.

These results support screening only; design qualification is not established. Transfer of calibration to the invented geometry is assumed; continuous fill coverage and anti-roll phase remain unestablished. The anti-roll benefit on a real vessel is not established. See Section 7.

  • Conduit loss: a calibrated area exponent of 2.138 fits the archived damping with 8.6 % RMS over 35 cases. The simple inverse-area law, refitted on its own, gives 36.5 % RMS.
  • Natural period: the calibrated model reproduces the CFD-derived exchange natural period within the published ±3 % band at four of five off-calibration checks. The low-fill check (25 %) is 3.7 % high. The calibration case agrees by construction (14.31 s against 14.31 s).
  • Response: in the illustrative screening prediction, with the tank, the predicted peak roll of the invented system falls from 10.0 to 5.7 per unit wave moment. The anti-roll benefit on a real vessel is not established.

Alpha is the normalized stiffness scale of the tank relative to the normalized hull restoring stiffness; it is distinct from tank-to-vessel mass ratio. The illustrative response uses alpha = 12.0 %, an ASSUMED input [I1] [I2].

2 Introduction

This study extends the analytical scope of the single-tank sloshing study to assess a U-tube style anti-roll arrangement: two connected tanks with invented geometry, joined by a conduit. The geometry represents no particular vessel or client. The connected-tank model is an analytical screening model calibrated on CFD assessment: the aggregate results of 35 cases from an earlier, archived CFD campaign on a separate twin-tank geometry. Analysis is performed to determine the connected-tank response and how closely the calibrated model reproduces the archived CFD; the key results are summarized in Section 1.

The audience is engineers assessing the analytical response and its evidence limits. Raw CFD fields, meshes and the archived geometry are outside this report; the illustrative configuration is distinct from the archived configuration.

3 Design data

The illustrative inputs define the calculated configuration; archived comparison conditions remain separate. Assumptions are marked below and their effects are listed in Appendix A.

3.1 Site or field data

Not applicable: the configuration is invented and has no site-specific basis.

3.2 Structure or equipment data

Invented round dimensions are selected independently of the published reference geometry [I2]. Validation of the illustrative plan areas and centroid offset is not established. Fill depth is an input; a validated fill-percentage range is not established.

The illustrative conduit area lies inside the published input range in the table. The calibrated effective length is transferred as an assumption; a measured natural period for the new geometry is required before predictive use, as described in the model calibration basis [I1].

3.3 Environmental data

No wave spectrum is specified. Fluid density is 1025 kg/m³ and gravity is 9.81 m/s², ASSUMED from the reference calculation constants [I1].

3.4 Vessel data

Vessel roll period 20.0 s, hull damping 5.0 % and alpha 12.0 % are ASSUMED from the reference response inputs [I2]. Dimensional vessel calibration is not established.

3.5 Criteria

The published ±3 % natural-period band is an archived comparison criterion, not a design acceptance limit [I3]. The moment-fit applicability is stated in Section 7; no operating envelope is established.

3.6 Load cases

The conduit-area and forcing-period sweeps use the inputs above. Imposed roll 5.0°, damping forcing period 20.0 s and level-difference amplitudes 0.1 m and 0.5 m are ASSUMED reference conditions [I2]. For the separate single-tank comparison, mass ratio μ = 0.05 and tuning ratio 1.0 are ASSUMED comparison inputs [I5]. The complete sweep matrix is in Appendix A.

4 Analysis methodology

The connected-tank model and the tuned-absorber model are evaluated at the illustrative inputs in Section 3. The archived CFD evidence is reported separately: the evidence record gives the source reduction, field and digest of each value, and raw fields and the archived geometry are excluded. The analytical scope follows the single-tank sloshing study; the connected-tank model is calibrated on its own.

The rigid-column energy balance provides the exchange natural period; quadratic conduit loss gives amplitude-dependent damping. Harmonic moment balance supplies the tank moment and coupled roll response. Frozen-fluid inertia is the roll inertia when the fluid is held fixed relative to the tank; it integrates the two prismatic legs and conduit; the separate tuned absorber illustrates peak splitting [I1] [I4].

Calculations use digitalmodel 2.1.0. The analytical implementation and archived CFD software-version gap are identified in [I6].

RMS denotes root mean square error; GCI denotes grid convergence index.

5 Results

Sections 5.1–5.3 report illustrative continuous model evaluations; Section 5.4 reports the separate discrete archived observations. Each figure provides its source reference, hover values and a CSV export.

5.1 Coupled roll response

With the tank, the predicted peak roll falls from 10.0 to 5.7 per unit wave moment (vessel roll period 20.0 s, hull damping 5.0 %, alpha 12.0 %); this is a screening prediction for the invented system.

The coupled response is evaluated with the published response inputs [I2]: vessel roll period 20.0 s, hull damping 5.0 % and alpha 12.0 %. Alpha denotes the normalized tank stiffness scale, distinct from a mass ratio. In the coupled-response model [I1], the forcing reference is fixed by the bare-vessel roll amplitude. The calculated response is roll per unit wave moment at that finite reference; quadratic loss makes it amplitude-dependent. Shading marks periods outside the published moment-fit band. Wave-spectrum and dimensional vessel calibration are not established.

5.2 Illustrative response curves

The connected-tank curves are evaluated using the analytical model [I1] at the illustrative inputs listed above. Frozen-fluid prismatic roll inertia is calculated in the inertia curve; a validation error for rigid-column conduit inertia is not established by that curve.

Damping is evaluated at forcing period 20.0 s with imposed level-difference amplitudes from the published damping inputs [I2]. The calculated damping depends on amplitude; it is not a fixed tank property. The largest plotted equivalent damping is 195.4 %: over-critical (above 100 %). It is an amplitude-dependent equivalent loss ratio, not a constant linear free-decay damping ratio. Percent axes divide by 100 to give the dimensionless ratio used in the archived comparisons.

The moment is calculated at 5.0° imposed roll and the illustrative conduit area, using the tank-moment model [I1].

5.3 Single-tank comparison: split and merging

The tuned-absorber model [I4] is evaluated at the frequency grid and damping values in the published response record [I5]. The mass ratio μ = 0.05 and frequency tuning ratio 1.0 are ASSUMED comparison inputs. A single equivalent tank is coupled to an undamped primary vessel. The tank is not isolated, and its geometry is not matched to the U-tube system.

5.4.1 Conduit-area sweep

Exchange amplitudes are compared at forcing period 6.25 s and imposed roll 5.0°. This is the imposed forcing condition of the archived area sweep, not a measured exchange natural period. The record does not establish why that forcing period was selected. Exchange amplitude is the volume displaced between the legs about its mean (m³). Ratios are normalized to the smallest area. The historical analytical amplitude uses geometric conduit length; it is not the later calibrated model.

5.4.4 Loss scaling and independent area check

The fitted area exponent is n = 2.138, with 8.6 % RMS over 35 cases. The naive inverse-area form has 36.5 % RMS after its own coefficient refit: it underpredicts damping at the smallest area (group RMS 55.1 %) and overpredicts at the largest (group RMS 108.3 %). These group RMS magnitudes are distinct from signed individual errors.

Conditions near each predicted natural period. The original inverse-area prediction uses the reference calibration, not the separate all-data coefficient refit.

At the independent intermediate area, the existing law evaluated without refitting gives 8.7 % RMS. Including that area in the fit gives n = 2.112 and 8.7 % RMS over 38 cases. Percentages are rounded to one decimal place; the evidence record retains the source precision. The independent prediction and all-data refit are separate checks.

5.4.5 Forced-roll period sweep and numerical checks

The medium-mesh forced-roll cases are accepted for screening after cycle convergence. The exchange plateau is the broad region of similar forced exchange amplitudes across adjacent forcing periods; it is separate from the exchange natural period. Fine-mesh confirmation applies at the selected period only; it does not establish convergence throughout the sweep.

Analytical screening cases are not CFD solves. Failed automated case-launch scripts and the open-boundary transfer check are rejected. Short transfer checks are verification only. Trustworthy phase and anti-roll benefit remain withheld. The evidence classification is in Appendix A.

6 Validation and benchmark

The calibration quantities below are reported in the model calibration summary [I1] and published calibration checks [I2]. RMS denotes root mean square error; each percentage applies to the corresponding reference fit.

Table 6.1 – Published calibration quantities
Published quantityValue
Quadratic conduit loss: calibrated area exponent2.138
Calibration cases (aggregate results only)35
Calibrated loss-law RMS (%)8.6
Refitted inverse-area law RMS (%)36.5
Closed-form moment RMS (%)4.3
Moment fit applies from forcing period (s)20
Degradation reported below about (s)16
Forced-sweep / natural-period calibrated effective length (times)2.76

The loss comparison is based on a separate refit of each area law, as documented in the calibration checks [I2]. A fixed-coefficient exponent substitution is excluded. Effective conduit length is calibrated against a measured natural period, as specified in the calibration basis [I1]; the forced-sweep peak is loss-controlled and varies with roll amplitude. The reported factor 2.76 is the effective length inferred from that forced-sweep peak divided by the length calibrated from the measured natural period [I1].

The archived CFD-derived periods and damping reductions are the completed comparison basis. They do not establish physical validation of the invented geometry. Validation of that geometry is planned against measured exchange natural period, moment and loss across roll amplitudes; those data are not supplied.

7 Limitations

These results support screening only; design qualification is not established. The limitations below govern interpretation of Section 5.

  • The moment fit holds for forcing periods of 20 s and longer (4.3 % RMS) and degrades below about 16 s; the cause is not established. See Appendix A.
  • Calibration transfer to the invented geometry remains an assumption even inside that band; a measured natural period is required before effective-length recalibration. See Section 3 and Appendix A.
  • The single-tank comparison does not match mass, tuning, hull damping and forcing; only peak splitting and merging are illustrated. See Section 5.3.
  • Continuous fill coverage, trustworthy anti-roll phase and anti-roll benefit remain unestablished. See Section 5.4.3 and Appendix A.
  • Archived period checks do not establish a frozen-fluid roll-inertia error bound; wave-spectrum and dimensional coupling evidence is absent. See Appendix A.
  • Fine-mesh confirmation applies only at the selected period; its Courant value exceeds the nominal target, and free-decay convergence is non-asymptotic with indicative GCI only. See Section 5.4.5.

8 Conclusions and next steps

Further assessment is required before the illustrative response is applied to a design. The geometry assumptions, comparison limits and calibration limits define the outstanding work below.

  • Not done: The new geometry's natural period requires measurement before effective conduit length is recalibrated.
  • Not done: Moment and loss require validation across roll amplitudes and the short-period band.
  • Not done: Single and connected tanks require comparison at matched mass, tuning, hull damping and forcing.
  • Not done: The residual cause requires resolution before the empirical validity band is widened.
  • Not done: Operating fill, freeboard, structural loads and dimensional vessel coupling require assessment.

The low-fill exception to the published period band requires natural-period measurement and recalibration before predictive use; the affected case and error appear in Figure 5.8. The comparison supports the stated analytical scope and does not qualify the invented illustrative geometry.

Evidence classes and supporting limitations

Wrapper cases are cases attempted through automated case-launch scripts. An End marker is the normal solver-completion message. Open transfer denotes the open-boundary transfer check, rejected because of boundary-flux growth. A screening manifest is a list of analytical screening cases; it does not establish completed CFD solutions [I3].

Appendix B – Reproduce commands

Execute the linked calculation command from the repository root with Python; it evaluates the analytical models without a CFD solver. Output locations and source files are listed in [I7].

python -m scripts.capabilities.build_dual_tank_sloshing_study
